transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’ve just been feeling really restless. Like I’m wound too tight and can’t quite settle down, even when I’m supposed to be sitting calmly in a meeting, or painting, or doing yoga. It’s been… hard to ignore.
Along with this restless feeling, have you also been experiencing a lot of worry or anxious thoughts running through your mind?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. It feels more like my body won’t settle than my mind racing with worries.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications recently, such as antipsychotics, antidepressants, or anti-nausea drugs?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t changed anything like that recently.
Have you noticed any other physical changes lately, like unexplained weight loss, a racing heartbeat, excessive sweating, or feeling unusually hot?
No… I haven’t really noticed anything like that. Nothing that stands out, anyway.
Have you been using any caffeine, energy drinks, recreational drugs, or other substances more than usual recently?
No… I mean, not more than usual. I might have coffee like I normally do, but nothing different that I can think of.
Thinking back, did you notice similar restlessness, fidgeting, or trouble sitting still when you were a child or teenager?

Yeah… I think so. In elementary school I remember getting notes sent home because I’d keep getting out of my seat, or I’d talk over other kids. I’d also blurt out answers before the teacher was even done asking.

Since those childhood experiences, have you continued to notice ongoing difficulties with staying focused, being easily distracted, or acting impulsively throughout your teenage and adult years, even during calm, non-stressful periods?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had times like that, but I can’t say I’ve tracked it consistently or that anything specific stands out right now.

Would people who know you well—like coworkers, friends, or family—say you've regularly struggled with staying focused or acting impulsively across different areas of your life, even outside of stressful situations?

I think… yes, probably. At work it’s come up with purchase orders needing corrections, and my planning coordinator has had to double-check things more than usual. At home, family dinners can get tense because they say I talk over people.

Over just the last six months, would you say these attention and impulsivity issues—like the purchase order mistakes or talking over people—have been happening consistently, nearly every day, rather than just occasionally?

Not nearly every day, exactly… but it’s been noticeably harder to manage for a while. I’d say about two years or so—maybe a little over—since the in-law conflicts started taking over more of our evenings.

Before the in-law conflicts started about two years ago, were you already experiencing this physical restlessness and inability to sit still, or did that specific feeling begin around the same time the conflicts started?

I think the restless feeling was there before, yes. It’s sort of this wound-up feeling, like I can’t fully settle even when I’m supposed to just sit through a planning meeting, or even doing something calm like painting or yoga. It’s just… hard to be still.
